utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, the witness is scheduled to be here for a long time in chief, so let us proceed as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for Mr. Milosevic. Microphone. Microphone, please. The microphone is not switched on. Could the microphone be turned towards Mr. Milosevic, please. It's facing right the other way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, proceed now, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope you have received a proper translation of tab 10, which we dealt with last week. I'll just dwell on that for a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, General. I hope you have tab 10 in front of you. It is the decision to establish a ministerial staff for the suppression of terrorism. What is the date of the decision? When was it passed?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision was passed on the 16th of June, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We have here the staff members appointed by the minister, and apart from that, it says here after listing all the individuals one by one that the expanded Staff shall also include chiefs of the Secretariats for Internal Affairs centres and branches of the RDB, Department of State Security, in the AP, autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that the expanded staff incorporates all these individuals as well as the chiefs of secretariats in the Kosovo and Metohija area, all of them?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, what is defined here as the staff's assignment?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Last time, I said that under II the task of the staff was defined, and it was defined in such a way as being tasked with planning, organising and managing the activities and use of the organisational units of the ministry, both the sent and attached units, to suppress terrorism in the area of the AP of Kosovo and Metohija. And then para 2, also the staff is tasked with planning, organising, directing, and coordinating the activities of the organisational units of the ministry in Kosovo and Metohija in carrying out complex security operations, special security operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In the documents here we have a number of these decisions on the staff for suppressing terrorism. Now, what is the difference between them?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference between these various decisions basically is in the personnel composition of the staff. Of course, the difference between this decision and the previous decision, if I remember that correctly, is negligible with respect to the mandates of the staff. This decision is focused more on the suppression of terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija and, therefore, the title of the staff, the name of the staff has been changed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, you said that we shall be tendering exhibits into evidence at the end of a tab. Is that how we're going to proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let us now continue with your testimony where you left off at the end of our last working session. I asked you whether there were any -- was there any overlapping in what the police and the army did.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that the overlapping of competencies in the negative sense did not exist but that the army carried out, pursuant to the rules governing the ministry of the interior just as the police did in conformity with the rules of resubordination, did tasks that came under the duties of the army and vice versa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain that to us more closely, please, bearing in mind several excerpts contained in tab 4 taken from the law on the army and the other relevant provisions, the law on defence, and other law in point.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can do that. In tab 4, on page 2, Article 30, para 1 of the law on the army of Yugoslavia says: "The rights and duties of authorised personnel of the organs of the interior in the army is performed by authorised personnel of the organs of security and the military police." Then Article 31, para 2, once again the law on the army of Yugoslavia, states the following: "Authorised persons in the service of the organs of security and military police may in performing their duties in the field of security or military police use firearms and other means as prescribed by separate provisions in conformity with the rules governing the organs of the interior." So this article deals with what military officials can use and others. Of course, these duties carried out by the organs of the military police and public security refers to military personnel. Now, Article 17 of the law on defence of Yugoslavia prescribes the means of resubordination of police units to the units of the army of Yugoslavia, how they are resubordinated and attached to them. But I think that we'll discuss this article at greater length in due course most probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Now, the army and the police, did they engage in joint operations; and if so, how did they engage in them? How did they carry them out?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The army and police in Kosovo and Metohija in the course of 1998 and 1999 had joint operations to suppress terrorism. Those operations were conducted according to a uniform, united plan for the suppression of terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija, and according to individual plans or, rather, orders for each specific operation and action.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, would you please take a look now at tabs -- you mentioned orders just now.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So -- now, please take a look at tab 145 onwards, and then I shall be asking you some questions pertaining to some of the material there, some of these documents. Tab 145 contains one such order. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I'd like us to look at tabs 146, 145, 7, 8, and 9, now, please. This is a document --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No translation for any of these, unless the Chamber's been provided with more material than I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, any explanation?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, my information tells me that this has been translated. However -- well, anyway, I hope that the general will briefly be able to explain this. We can place it on the ELMO. And I will check during the break what material has already arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. It's relatively short, so it may be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's take the portions that have been translated. Tab 148 has been translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If it has been translated, why is it we don't have the translation? That's right. We don't have the original either. We don't have the original.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll investigate during the break and see what all that is about, Mr. Robinson, check it out. But let's go back to tab 145, since it's a brief document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, in your index, beside tab 148 is the following: "Requested document not yet received from the authorities in Belgrade." How does that tie in with the explanation that you give?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I have here is it says tab 148, in English, the 24th of May, 1999. Probably in the meantime what happened, that document came in. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, do you have that document, document tab 148? Do you have it in the Serbian?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in the Serbian version, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: How long is the document, how many pages?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document, I have it here in English, is four pages long.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the English version be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we're going to lose time because of the maladministration of your case, but let the English version be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It's tab 148, General. You can follow it in the Serbian, the copy in front of you. Have you found tab 148?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have. Do you want me to say something?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Just quote the characteristic points, what you think should be highlighted. All the documents we find in 146, 7, 8, and 9.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In all these tabs, what we have are orders, the ones that I mentioned in responding to your previous question, and those orders relate to disbanding --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt, but can we see the title of this document. It looks like the ones already exhibited. "Order." Thank you. Yes. Proceed, Mr. Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Judge. In tab 148, just like in the other tabs, we have a series of orders of the command of the Pristina Corps to disband and destroy, or break up and destroy the Siptar operations in different operations and different geographical regions. This tab 148 specifically is an order. It is an order to break up and destroy the Siptar terrorist forces in the Lipovica sector. The date is the 24th of May, 1999, and of course its contents or, rather, the contents of this order have been standardised. It is the customary way in which these orders are written for things of this kind. From this particular order we can see that in the anti-terrorist operations, specifically this particular operation, was one in which the joint forces of the army and police took part. And of course this can be seen straight away on point 2 of page 1 where the main tasks of the units are specified, and in line 1, if I can read it out, it says: "The 15th Armoured Brigade, together with parts of the 124th MUP Intervention Brigade (3 companies), the 36th Detachment of the special police units (3 companies) --" and then the next portion is not easy to read but quite obviously it refers to tasks for units of the police and army in that same anti-terrorist operation. Of course, in continuation, once again it is a standardised form, we have the tasks that are specified in the usual manner. All the other tabs that you mentioned are very similar, with the proviso that they refer, of course, to other operations and are usually titled "Zapovest," "Order," rather than the word "Naredjenje," as is the case in tab 148.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, these orders in tabs 145, 6, 7, 8, and 9 all pertain to anti-terrorist activities where the army and police operated in concert?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It all has to do with anti-terrorist operations. But they are carried out at different points in time and in different areas. Different military and police units take part in them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The order in tab 145 bears which date?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order in tab 145 is dated the 25th of May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What about the next tab?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the 27th of May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tab 147?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 24th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Oh, the 24th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what about 149?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 149 is the 22nd of May, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: During the NATO aggression against the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, was there any resubordination of the police units to the army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was resubordination of the police to the army of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, but this response requires a detailed explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Through questions we'll try to get to that. First of all, the resubordination of the police to the army, is that something that regulations envisage at all, and was it limited in terms of its tasks and the area involved?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. In the law on the defence of the FRY, and that is Article 17 that we mentioned a few minutes ago, in accordance with that article, an order was passed on the resubordination of the forces and organs of the interior to the army of Yugoslavia. However, as I already said, that resubordination was limited in terms of its tasks because it pertained only to carrying out combat operations or, rather, anti-terrorist operations. Also, it was limited in terms of the police units involved because it pertained to specific police units only. In accordance with the orders that we have just seen, those were the police units that were involved in individual operations. In addition to that, resubordination was limited in terms of the area and time involved. That is to say that the resubordination of police units to the army can be reduced to the adoption of a plan for carrying out anti-terrorist operations and also issuing orders that we quoted in response to the previous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, I asked you about the regulations and you mentioned Article 17 of the law on the defence of Yugoslavia. That is contained in tab 4. I'm going to quote it very briefly. All of it has been translated.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the interpreters please have a reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, the interpreters just asked for a reference so that they can follow you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Tab 4, page 2, Article 17 of the law on defence of Yugoslavia, the one that the witness mentioned in response to my question whether there were any regulations pertaining to resubordination, and he indicated that particular article of the law on defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Before you proceed, I wanted to ask the witness, and perhaps you but more the witness, is there any special significance in the word "resubordination"? Why not just "subordination"? "Re" in English has a specific connotation; subordinating again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, of course these are synonyms. They have the same meaning but that is quite simply the wording in the law.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, the MUP units are subordinated to their commands, but in case of a threat of war, the law envisages that they should be resubordinated to the army in terms of possible combat operations within the zones of command of the army. I don't know whether "resubordination" is the best solution possible, but anyway, that is the word that is used. The wording of the law is rather clear, so I think that will make it clearer for you. It says: "In the event of imminent threat of war, a state of war, a state of emergency, internal affairs units and organs may be used to carry out combat tasks, provide support for combat or offer armed resistance. In carrying out their combat tasks, these units and organisations shall be subordinated to the Yugoslav army officer who is in command of combat operations." Subordination. Subordination to the officer of the army of Yugoslavia who is in command of combat operations. That is the wording of this provision. As far as regulations are concerned, that is the legal basis for resubordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, in relation to the resubordination of the police to the army, was there any problem involved, General?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it can be said that there were certain problems which primarily boiled down to a different interpretation of documents on subordination and resubordination, especially at lower levels, both in the army and in the police. However, after certain consultations were carried out in terms of these different interpretations of the mentioned documents were overcome. And as I said, subordination or resubordination was reduced to planning anti-terrorist operations by the military commands and issuing orders in order to carry out joint operations by the military and police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did resubordination pertain to all forms of police work and all police units or police units that take part in combat operations or, rather, in this combat against terrorism in the zone of responsibility of the commander of the unit to which they were subordinated? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course resubordination pertained only to specific tasks, specific units and only while these tasks were still under way in a given area. Apart from that, both the military and the police carried out their own tasks or, rather, those belonging to their own province of work. They had horizontal coordination throughout, though. That is to say exchange of information, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, General. We saw what this was like in the regulations as we saw this brief paragraph in tab 4. Could we please see what this looked like in practical terms. We have tabs 45, 46, 7, 8, 9, 50, and 51. So could you please take a look at tab 45 now. It's just one page.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This is the -- this is an order of the commander of the Pristina Corps --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: -- dated the 20th of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, again this is not translated.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can put it on the overhead projector. I believe it was translated, though. Perhaps it wasn't grouped properly, but I'm quite sure that all these documents were translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Tab 46 is translated.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the speaker, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters cannot hear anything. The microphone has not been switched on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please have the microphone switched on. Who switches it on; Mr. Milosevic or the control room? Yes. Will the control room please have the microphone of Mr. Milosevic switched on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's on now. I see that it's on now. I see that the light is on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead, General.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order of the commander of the Pristina Corps that has to do with the subordination of the units and the organs of the MUP of Serbia in the zones of responsibility of the brigades. It is dated the 20th of April, 1999. And it also invokes, in the preamble, the order of the staff of the Supreme Command, and it issues an order which we explained a bit earlier on. Point 1 says: "Units and organs of the interior of the MUP of Serbia in the zones of responsibility of the brigades shall be resubordinated to commands of brigades for carrying out combat tasks." That was point 1. Point 2: "In accordance with the organisation of the organs and units of the MUP and the deployment in the territory of the zone of responsibility of the brigades, plans of use should regulate concrete obligation in carrying out combat operations according to levels of command." Is it necessary for me to read on?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I would just like to draw your attention to the second paragraph of paragraph 4: "At the time when combat operations are not carried out, the forces of the MUP shall be engaged in carrying out other specific tasks according to the plans and orders of the staff of the MUP of -- for Kosovo and Metohija."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, can we conclude that all these orders from tabs 41 through 51 are quite a precise concretisation of this resubordination?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these tabs from tab 45 onwards, including 1950 -- including 51, actually pertain to this order of -- on resubordination and spell it out in more concrete terms, if I can put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The resubordination of the police in the area of operations of a certain brigade, that means that the unit of police within the zone of operations of a particular brigade is resubordinated to the commander of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in terms of carrying out the tasks we mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Only in terms of the specific tasks mentioned?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They respect their own chain of command with regard to all other tasks and they act independently of the army in all other respects?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can just add one thing; that policework was not resubordinated to the army in any way. There were certain interpretations when we discussed problems, that it was necessary to resubordinate the entire police jurisdiction to the army, which was not logical at all and that was not the underlying idea of this order. So in wartime, practically the police carried out all its work as in peacetime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I hope that this was sufficiently explained now. General, now we're going to move on to a different subject, a new subject. It has to do with the joint command in Kosovo and Metohija. I'm going to put a very specific question to you. Please listen to it carefully. Do you know that during 1998 and 1999 a command organ called the Joint Command was operating in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely speaking and briefly speaking, there was not that kind of organ called the Joint Command in Kosovo and Metohija in 1998 and in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. So there wasn't a command organ.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And had you heard this word "Joint Command" in relation to this period in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have heard of that, but of course it did not pertain to any kind of command organ. It represented something completely different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So it was not a command organ. What was it? You say that it was something completely different. What was it in actual fact?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The term "Joint Command" in Kosovo and Metohija during 1998 until the Verification Mission was established in Kosovo and Metohija, the term was used for horizontal coordination and cooperation among military police organs and state organs at all levels. In a practical sense, this joint command represented a series of meetings that were attended by representatives of the military, the police, and the state organs. At these meetings they exchanged information and data that were of relevance to all the participants. And after these meetings, everybody went back to their own line of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, this form of cooperation, you explained just now that this term was used. It was used regularly, that's my understanding on the basis of what you've said just now, in 1998, until the Verification Mission arrived, and that was the method of work actually.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can be put that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So horizontal cooperation among organs, was that your explanation?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. That's what the term denoted. It could also be explained if we say horizontal coordination in every way, but there is certainly no subordination or resubordination involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Did you attend any of those meetings of this coordination that was called the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, about ten or so, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. This form of cooperation under that term, did it go beyond the chain of command in any way, either in the police or in the military, or did it in any way infringe upon the regular chain of command either in the army or in the police?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it didn't. This horizontal cooperation or coordination did not infringe upon the chain of command either in the army or in the police in any way. Everybody consistently observed their own vertical chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, I'm asking you these questions because an allegation was made here that this term "Joint Command" represented some sort of command body that was outside the vertical chain of command in the army and in the police. Do you have any information to the effect that this coordination between the police, the army, and state organs in Kosovo went in any way beyond or outside the regular chain of command as envisaged by the law?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All chains of command at the time in Kosovo and Metohija were in conformity with legal provisions. This method of work, therefore, this type of coordination, did not affect in any way of normal chain of command either in the police or in the army, it only contributed to the better functioning of both forces because of frequent exchange of information about the situation on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: For this occasion, just to clarify this allegation that this form of work was somehow outside the normal of -- normal chain of command, I would like you to look at tab 144. That is -- actually, those are minutes of a meeting in my office that took place on the 2nd of November, 1998. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Give me just a second. I found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We will come back later to this document when discussing some other issues. For the moment, I only want to use this document to establish whether it shows clearly that all the bodies involved are within the chain of command, not outside of it. So I will ask you a couple of questions. It says here at the very beginning -- and these are minutes drawn up by the chef de cabinet. At the very beginning we see the order of contributions by various speakers who make proposals that will eventually become proposals of the Joint Command. So does it say proposals of the Joint Command? I opened this meeting, and after me spoke the commander of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We haven't got it translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's not translated, and I see it runs to 15 pages.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So that if it's going to be referred to, with the Court's leave, at all, it should be on the overhead projector so we know what we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we'll allow you to refer to it. You can refer to short passages, but it has to be on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Place page 1 on the ELMO. At the bottom of the page, we see an entry. Could you scroll it down a little. Now we can see the whole page. Please leave it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It says: "The commander of the Pristina Corps, Lieutenant General Nebojsa Pavkovic, gave a summary report on the implementation of the plan for combatting terrorism in Kosovo and Metohija and suggested a draft conclusion," et cetera, et cetera. This passage mentions this term "Joint Command," because it says in the second paragraph, "Speaking on behalf of the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija." Please, do not lose this upper part on the ELMO where the participants in the meeting are enumerated. General, at the time when he is making this report, General Pavkovic is a member of the Pristina Corps?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I just want to show the chain of command. Is he subordinated to the commander of the 3rd Army?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what about the commander of the 3rd Army? Is he subordinated to the commander of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So in this passage where General Pavkovic is reporting on these matters, is the commander of the 3rd Army present?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's Lieutenant General Dusan Samardzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Sixth line from the top, Lieutenant General Dusan Samardzic, commander of the 3rd Army. And above him is the Chief of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At the time it was Momcilo Perisic, Colonel General.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And so it is stated in the first paragraph. In the military chain of command, all the links above Pavkovic are present, such as the commander of the 3rd Army, to whom he reports personally; the Chief of the General Staff is present as well; and of course the president of the republic to whom the Chief of the General Staff reports. Is the chain of -- is this the complete chain of command?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. All the links in the chain of command are present, in the military chain of command.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let me just see where the next passage is, on which page. Page 7.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stevanovic, were you at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was, Your Honour. We can see that from this introductory part, line 3 from the top. Line 3 from the bottom of paragraph 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: We saw who was present on behalf of the entire military chain of command from the commander of the Pristina Corps to the president of the republic. Now, let us see on page 7. We see there was a contribution by Major General Sreten Lukic, who was a general of the police force. As we saw in that decision in tab 10, he was commander of the MUP staff.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. So he is speaking at this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, let us go back to page 1. Is it the case that this meeting was attended by Colonel General Vlastimir Djordjevic, who is directly above Sreten Lukic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: He was head of the public security sector?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And his direct superior, Minister of the Interior Vlajko Stojiljkovic is also present?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is, but I can't find him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The fifth line from the top of the paragraph. Minister of the Interior of the Republic of Serbia Vlajko Stojiljkovic.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is the president of the Republic of Serbia, Milan Milutinovic, also present?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Of course the meeting was attended by you as well and other participants on behalf of public and military security -- civilian and military security, that is. Let us look at the chain of command, however. Are all the links in the chain above Lukic present, from himself to the president of the republic?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not a single link in the chain was omitted.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I hope this is enough by way of response to the allegation that there was something outside of the chain of command, particularly this type of coordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I will now move on to a different subject, General. It concerns local security or, rather, local police and confidence-building measures in Kosovo and Metohija. Could you tell us, please, what is understood by the term of "local security" in Kosovo and Metohija, and what was the purpose and the intent of establishing local security in this area?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Local security in Kosovo and Metohija implied a specially organised system of engagement of local Albanians for the purpose of maintaining public law and order and some other affairs within their local communities. The establishment of such a system of local security was geared at building up the confidence between local Albanian communities and members of the police force, the MUP, of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, who were the members of this local police force or local security?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the local security were Albanians who accepted to work in the local police on the terms and conditions stipulated by a contract that they signed with organs of local self-management.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please look at tab 26. This document provides us with a very specific list of a local police such as in the municipality of Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. That is a list of the local police force in the municipality of Djakovica at a certain point in time. I would like to ask that names of individuals not be mentioned here for their own safety.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, those names were well known at the time, but it is entirely appropriate that you should ask for this protective measure, and I hope Mr. Robinson will grant it.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we have two lists. One is horizontal, the other is vertical. The names are the same but they are arranged slightly differently. From this first list we can see their names, the village they were in charge of, their registration number, the type of uniform they had, and the weapon they had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I understand that you have requested that the names not be mentioned. You have to provide a reason, because this is a public trial, as you know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Stevanovic indicated that Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. individuals -- that those who survived, although I believe most of these people have been killed, could experience problems because they used to be local policemen, and as such they were targets of the KLA during the entire time of terrorist activities and after 2000, after 1999 as well. I suppose that is the reason why the general is suggesting that their names not be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, do you --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I am afraid I'm at a loss to understand the reasoning. It seems to me these men were well known at the time and I can't see any reason for them not to be named now. I can't see what the risk is in their being identified as to what they were doing at the time, which must have been well known at the time. There it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It's surely for the accused, though, to decide how he presents this, and if he wants to do it by using the numbers, what can anyone do about it?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: If he wants to do it by using the numbers and if he persuades the Chamber not to lay the document on the overhead projector, and if I don't raise the question of the names specifically in cross-examination, then Your Honour is quite right, but is that an appropriate way to get around the requirement that the material should basically be public unless good reason is shown for it to be dealt with otherwise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if you allow me, I could try to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I did not suppose that this was going to be complicated, but bearing in mind the fact that these people were well known in their areas, wore the uniforms of the police, we can make their names public. My only intention, my only thought was to protect individuals from possible problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well. Well, we'll proceed in the normal way.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We will continue in the normal way, but out of consideration for these people, I will skip their names, which of course imposes no obligation on Mr. Nice to do the same, but I'm going to make sure that I not the cause of any problems for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, here we see, village by village, the names of these policemen. There are mainly two per village. So in the first list there is a total of 30 villages in that municipality alone, the municipality of Djakovica, where the local police functioned.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. The big numbers denote villages, and the smaller number next to it in the next column is the number of the member of the local security.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is self-explanatory. We also see the registration number of every member of the local police and information whether his uniform was drawn from supplies and the type of pistol also drawn from supplies. In this case that is the 7.65 millimetre pistol. So this is a list for the municipality of Djakovica. Now, tell me, General, in those places where local security was established as we see in the list under tab 26, was there any need for members of the MUP to be present?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that need was considerably reduced once the local security was established. The police, of course, continued to do their regular work but with considerably smaller presence in those areas where the local police maintained public law and order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So in those villages where there was no special reason for them to go in, the police did not enter?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said at the beginning that the basic object of this whole system was precisely that the local Albanians should come to understand that the police had no goal of being present in the village itself but that their goal was to provide law and order in the village. Now, if they accepted keeping law and order, then the police accepted to go there only when the need arose or, rather, in cases where members of the local forces were not able to or did not have the authority to get a job done with respect to a given event.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell us, please, in what way, under what conditions were the members of the local security recruited and engaged?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the local security were recruited and engaged under this system according to the principle on voluntariness. That is to say if they accepted the conditions stipulated in the agreement drawn up by the organs of self-government, and those contracts or agreement specified their rights and duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's take a look at one of those contracts or agreements, tab 24. And the date of that one is the 1st of January, 1999. So it is a contract between the individual that is becoming a local policeman by entering into the contract.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. This contract defines the person's rights and duties, and it is the person entering into the contract with a representative of local self-government. In this case, it was the president of the Municipal Assembly of Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. Fine. Now, the locals of a village, the villagers in which this local police force was established, did they have any influence on the election of the members of that local police force or were those names put forward from outside?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In principle, it was up to them to represent their own representatives, people they trusted and people who would be able to represent their interests vis-a-vis the police and local self-government authorities. And we'll see this from one of the subsequent exhibits. I can't remember which one it is just now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, take a look at this particular contract. Let's do that. We have the name and surname of the person entering into the contract, and then it says, "Relates to security," and then 1, it says, infrastructure; 2, health protection; 3, food supplies; 4 maintaining public law and order. That is a classical task that the police does. Control and registering people who are coming into the area or passing through the area, and generally providing conditions for the normal life and work of the citizens or villagers.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was -- those were the basic duties for which they were remunerated and engaged in the first place. Looking at it from the security related issues, point 4 the most important one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. Now, point 3, or article 3, it says the coordinator of local security - that applies to each one - has an ID in order to present his ID to third persons.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So he has a sort of police card or a similar document?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. And I think that we have attached a copy of the type of ID they would carry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is in tab 25, a photocopy of the kind of identification papers that we mean. Could the photocopy be placed on the overhead projector. The first page need not be placed on the ELMO, but would you please read out what it says. On the reverse as well as on the first side it says the Republic of Serbia. It says that in Serbian and Albanian. Is that what it says, the Republic of Serbia? Then it says in Albanian Republic of Serbia, and then underneath it says the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija, and then that same thing in Albanian, the autonomous province of Kosovo and Metohija in Albanian, in the two languages, Serbian and Albanian.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Then it says local security, both in Serbian and in Albanian once again. Then it says municipality in Albanian and Serbian, the village in Serbian and Albanian, the first and last name, and the number.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, what does it say on the reverse side of the ID for this local security? Could you read it out, please, in Serbian. And the text is the same in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reverse side of the ID says as follows -- it is written in Serbian and Albanian. In Serbian, it reads as follow: "The bearer of this identity card is authorised to work to secure the infrastructure, to provide health care protection, food supply, law and order, maintenance, and other conditions for the normal life of citizens, to issue warnings, to check identity documents, to arrest persons, to use force and to carry a firearm." So those are the tasks and competencies which have been entered into the ID card for the local security personnel and taken from the contract.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So he can take persons into custody, use force, and carry firearms; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, please, General, the members of the local police, did they wear a uniform?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did. However, the uniforms were made in a continuous period, or, rather, they didn't have uniforms to begin with until they were supplied with a uniform. However, it was envisaged that each member of the local security service should have and should wear uniforms, and most of them did. And we can see that from the list we read out a moment ago, looked at a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: According to that list, all of them wore uniforms -- most of them.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did that uniform differ in any way from the police uniform?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in slight details but I can't go into the details now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But it could be distinguished. You could distinguish a local policeman from a policeman which was a policeman employed by the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Just like this ID card differs in certain aspects to a police ID.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And where was this idea on local security first applied? Where did it start from?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It came from the municipality of Djakovica and that's where it proved most successful. Of course, the activities -- activities along those lines were organised in other municipalities as well or, rather, in all the municipalities with an Albanian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And what were the work results of the members of the local security that we mentioned here and talked about?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the police force, we were satisfied with their work. They worked satisfactorily. First of all, because the police had to go to those villages less frequently, on rarer occasions, and that was one of the goals for which this whole system was established in the first place. And there were very specific, concrete results that the members of the local security force had to do with respect to reporting any violations, uncovering the perpetrators of crimes, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I'd like to draw your attention to tab 27 now, please, where we can see a document dated December. It is a letter sent to the staff of the Ministry of the Interior, and it says the chief of the secretariat from Djakovica for purposes of local security, winter uniforms must be issued as well as wind jackets, shirts, pants, and so on. And we saw on the basis of a previous document that they had already received weapons. So this entire equipment is listed here.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. The local security force was established with cooperation between the provisional Executive Council, the staff of the MUP in Kosovo and Metohija, and the local self-government authorities. And the police force gave them logistical support and professional support, and here we can see that it was the police that supplied them with uniforms. You can't actually see that but they did also supply weapons for the local security force.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So this document is important because it is dated 1998. There are, of course, earlier documents in 1998 as well.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, as a confidence-boosting measure, did this have a positive effect on the situation in the villages where the local security force was established?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, because with the establishment of a local security force, the imposed thoughts among the citizens that the police was repressive was done away with, and that the force -- police force came into villages just for repressive measures. We managed to show the local Albanians that that was not the goal of the police force but that they were bent on providing law and order in their villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Law and order that they could keep themselves, enforce themselves to the best of their ability. And did they -- were they able to do that?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can we see some examples of the results scored by the local security force? And I draw your attention to tabs 28 to 35 in that respect.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In these tabs we have several examples of the concrete work and conduct of the local security force in keeping with the authorisations specified in the contract we looked at a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In tab 28, we see a report by the SUP of Djakovica about the fact that a member of the local security force was subject to serious threats and that the perpetrator, in conformity with the law, was sanctioned with a misdemeanour charge.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, what else do we see? We see that --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We see that a member of the local security force in the next document reported to the duty service in Djakovica, that on the 1st of May, 1999, at around 2200 hours, in the house of a villager, that three unidentified persons entered the house of Vitor Docaj of Yugoslavia armed with automatic rifles. So this is an example where members of the local force call in members of the Yugoslav army. They report conducts on the part of members of the Yugoslav army.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In this case, the policeman was an Albanian?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This Albanian policeman, in fact on the 1st of May, 1999; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Although the date is the 2nd of May. That was the time when, according to what is presented here, the Albanians were allegedly expulsed and terror being effected against them. So on the 1st of May, 1999, this particular Albanian, a member of the local security force, was reporting to the police the conduct of three -- inappropriate conduct of three Yugoslav soldiers who tried to abuse the female family member of a given family.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And we can see that pursuant to that report the organs of the police were notified about that and that the police took steps to apprehend the perpetrators of that particular offence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And all this is taking place on the 1st of May, 1999. That is to say, the local security force is functioning properly; it is reporting the misconduct of soldiers and the appropriate authorities are taking steps to act upon his report. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, take a look at tab 30, please. Here we can see that on the 13th of May, once again it is the Djakovica municipality area, where a member of the local security force, once again an Albanian, took into custody another Albanian whom he caught thieving.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So once again the time is mid-May, the time of the aggression, when it is assumed that Albanians were being expelled from Kosovo and Metohija. Here we have an Albanian member of the local security force who catches a thief, is taking him to the local police station. We can see all that from this Official Note, which has its number, and the date is the 13th of May, 1999. Then we come to the next tab, tab 31, which is a receipt for items confiscated.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Relating to the previous case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's right, because he was caught red handed, and the items that the person had stolen were confiscated, and this is a receipt for that, and the date on the receipt is once again the 30th of May, 1999. So two months after the aggression. Now take a look at tab 32. The date there is the 15th of May. What is important here is --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, once again a person was taken into custody by a member of the local security force because they were found --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes. He was engaged in an act and was apprehended by a local Albanian police force, and that is mid-May that we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It is in fact the 15th of May, 1999; is that right?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Take a look at tab 33 now, please. This is an Official Note. It is dated the 16th of May, and once again a local Albanian policeman who took into custody and brought into the police station a certain individual, once again an Albanian. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. But this is important, because a member of the local security force in actual fact took into custody an individual whom it was supposed had taken part in the killing of several policemen in the period gone by.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Right. So that means that a member of the local security force, on the 16th of May, 1999, that is to say two months -- almost two months into the aggression and the alleged persecution of Albanians, here we have an Albanian bringing in somebody who he had taken into custody, taking him to the police force -- police station concerning a murder that had been committed earlier.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, take a look at tab 34. The date there is the 19th of May.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the case where a weapon was confiscated from a citizen in cooperation with members of the local security force in this particular village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So we have a member of a local security team reporting and confiscating somebody -- confiscating a rifle that had been hidden and dug into the ground, and the person was found in illegal possession of that weapon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, what do you say this -- all this evidence indicates? Just very briefly.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite clearly, Mr. Robinson, these confidence-building measures and the appointment of Albanian policemen in purely Albanian villages was operational, and it denies, by virtue of the fact that it was there, that Albanians were persecuted. They were there. They carried weapons. They wore uniforms. So this is quite contrary to what the side opposite has been saying, that the police were expelling Albanians and killing them. This is a series of examples to the contrary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to draw your attention to the dates that are very important on these documents. All of this happened in mid-May, all the documents we provided here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So we have tab 35 to deal with as well. That was compiled around the 19th of May too. It also has to do with the work of the local security. Do you think that there is anything characteristic that has to be highlighted in this respect, General?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's quite similar to the previous examples. Members of the local security informed us that the following persons were caught stealing in the said village. So the police was informed by the local security that some persons in the mentioned village were involved in stealing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, General. What kind of effect did the NATO aggression have on the operation of local security?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly had a negative effect on this system of local security, because many members of the local security suffered the retaliation of terrorists, because the police were not in a position to protect them any more as they were before when their safety was in jeopardy.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please look at tab 84, General. What happened? What was written here to the secretariat in Kosovo and Metohija by the head of the MUP staff in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No translation, Mr. Milosevic. If it's brief, it may be put on the ELMO. Let's have it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Just give us some brief comments with regard to this. So the NATO aggression was under way. What happened to Albanians then? How did they react and how did the police react?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd of May, 1999, is the date of this document. It was written by the staff of the Ministry of the Interior, and it was sent to the Secretariats of the Interior in Kosovo and Metohija. It has to do with the reporting of residence of citizens so that they can be taken care of. This has to do with the regulation of the population that left their places of residence. But one of the measures in paragraph 2 -- sorry. No, not paragraph 2. It's paragraph 3, subparagraph 4. So point 3 reads as follows: "Persons who reside in a particular area should be protected from a security and safety point of view and they should be familiarised with their obligations and ensure," and now under 4: "to appoint a representative who will carry out the work of the local police and carry out contacts with the authorities in order to resolve humanitarian issues and issues related to their safety and security, the provision of food, water, electricity, and other matters of relevance to the normalisation of life and work in their places of residence." This document practically issues an order to secretariats to communicate with the local communities by affecting them in that way, namely, that they should appoint their own representatives who would be involved in this line of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So that they should appoint their own local policemen?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Who would take care of law and order among them.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are these internally displaced persons who moved from a particular territory because of combat operations?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. These are persons who were staying outside their places of permanent residence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And why were they outside their permanent places of residence, General?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is quite clear that that was because of the combat operations in Kosovo and Metohija, that they had to move from the areas where they lived, and also for other reasons that I could perhaps explain in greater detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What was the attitude of the KLA towards the representatives of this local security and do you know what the fate was of the members of the local security when the army, our army and police, withdrew from Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the members of the so-called KLA certainly had a negative attitude towards the members of the local security because it did not suit them to have any kind of confidence building between the local Albanians and the police. Conflicts, hatred, intolerance were things that actually suited them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, General, in addition to the establishment of this local community -- local security, what other measures were taken at the time, at the height of the crisis during the war? What other measures were taken by the Ministry of the Interior vis-a-vis the Albanian population? What other confidence-building measures?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not only in times of war. As a matter of fact, from mid-1998 onwards, the police of Serbia tried in Kosovo and Metohija in many ways to convince the Albanians that there was no reason for them to be afraid of regular, everyday police work. In that sense, members of the police even refrained from using roads where there could be conflicts. And they also refrained from entering villages, especially Albanian villages where it was assumed that certain conflicts might break out. After that, and also in relation to that, the police, whenever possible, took a series of actions in order to return all internally displaced persons to their places of permanent residence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Before we move on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Obviously with this number of documents I'm not going to be able to return to all or even many of the documents in cross-examination. This particular document, 84, has no English translation, and it is on its face in need of some explanation. It's not stamped, it's not signed, it's not a photocopy of a sent document and I wonder if the Chamber, before allowing the accused to move on to the next document, would wish to get a little more detail of what exactly we're looking at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note a recent arrival contains the translation of 84.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Uh-huh. But again the original is different, I think, from many other originals because it looks as much like a draft as anything else, and I'm grateful to -- and pleased to know that there is now a translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let us have some information from the witness on the provenance of this document. General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President of the Trial Chamber, I have indeed noticed that there aren't any signatures or stamps here, but I do know with certainty that this document was adopted and was sent on to the secretariats. At that time I was in Kosovo and Metohija and I know that action was taken by all secretariats on the basis of this document. I know that in the Ministry of the Interior of Serbia there is a document that would bear a stamp and signature or some other proof that this document was sent out in order to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Milosevic, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The Ministry of the Interior, the staff of the ministry, and then it says, "12a Strictly Confidential number 14, 2 May, 1999."

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Obviously there's a number there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And here it says, "Head of Staff, General Sreten Lukic," and that was typed out. Is that because it was sent as a dispatch, as a telegram to everyone?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's obvious that it's a document of the staff. You can see the date, you can see the number; the only thing missing here is an authentic signature. But I assert that this is a document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, General, yes. I think we have enough information. Proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, in your previous answer you mentioned that the staff of the ministry or, rather, the police in Kosovo and Metohija organised the return of internally displaced persons. Did you personally have an opportunity of participating in any such activity? Were you present when such activity was carried out related to the return of internally displaced persons to their homes?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Sometime in the summer or autumn 1998, I myself spent four or five days in the village of Istinic in the municipality of Decani. After terrorist activities, tens of thousands of Albanians had moved there. They were internally displaced persons. It was very hot there, I remember, although it was already well into the autumn. I remember that three or four -- for three or four days the local government vehicles were engaged in order to return all the Albanians to their homes, to their places of residence. On that occasion in that large group of Albanians there were many terrorists with weapons, and after specific negotiations with some of the prominent local Albanians, we managed to convince them that they should hand over their weapons, that they should not fear for their safety, that they would all be returned to their homes, although they possessed weapons. To be very brief, on that occasion they handed in perhaps over 2.000 pieces of weapons, including military equipment. They were returned to their homes at the time. So at that moment, this problem which threatened to grow into humanitarian catastrophe was overcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In this document that we mentioned a few moments ago, the one in tab 84, in paragraph 3 it says in the first subparagraph that you did not quote because you quoted the establishment of local security, but here it says: "Persons who are residing at a particular place should be protected," et cetera, and then subparagraph 1 is that: "they should hand over weapons, ammunition, and military equipment which they were forced to receive from terrorists..." They could hand it over without any consequences. Does this mean that they would not be held accountable by anyone even though they would hand in weapons?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. They were very frightened that they would suffer consequences because they had weapons. However, in order to resolve the more serious problem at hand, namely, to return them to their homes, our minimum requirement was that weapons be handed over without the persons who possessed the weapons suffering any consequences. I can just mention that while working in Istinic, I had a certain problem with the representatives of I think the members of the International Red Cross. And in one of these dispatches I think we can find the name of this person who did everything in his or her power to persuade the Albanians that they should not leave Istinic, and that they were the safest there and that they may be the victims of violence in their own village. That was highly unusual, and I strongly protested in this case, but persistently in various corners here and there in -- they were trying to persuade the Albanians that what we were doing was wrong. However, within a few days we did manage to persuade the Albanians that they should go back home.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have to take the break now, but before we take it, just tell me, what was the response to the offer to have them hand over weapons without suffering any consequences? Were any weapons handed over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I didn't explain it properly. I said specifically in Istinic. As far as I can remember, around 3.000 different pieces of weaponry were handed over. And later on, we were always in a position to receive from citizens weapons that they had handed over themselves. This will probably become evident on the basis of various documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll now take a break of 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, what did the police do in this entire period, 1998 and 1999, with regard to the reporting of temporary residence by citizens and with regard to providing temporary accommodation?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said a couple of things about this. I can only say more specifically that both in 1998 and 1999 every effort was made so that people who were residing outside of their homes temporarily returned to their homes. Staffs for combatting terrorism and police secretariats in Kosovo and Metohija undertook during the war, I believe sometime in May, to have accommodation provided for all internally displaced people and to have them report their temporary residence so as to ensure precise statistics and for proper accommodation to be provided with precise information about who is residing where. This was reflected in a document we recently had on the overhead projector. That was an order issued to secretariats specifying what the secretariats were supposed to do in terms of organised activity aimed at reporting the residence of internally displaced persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Was this dictated by the need to provide accommodation and protect those people? What kind of danger were they in?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke about the reporting of temporary residence. However, the police also took steps to protect columns of people who were moving out of their places of residence from all sorts of danger, and there were all kinds of danger.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any reports or requests made by certain groups or villagers to provide protection?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my information, there were -- there were indeed individual requests from families to provide protection for their families in their movement from their homes to other places. I remember a visit by Mr. Rugova, Ibrahim Rugova, who wanted protection for his family which wanted to move to Macedonia from Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Several questions about the Verification Mission in Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just before moving on to that, are there records of the displaced personnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Records on newly reported residences are to be found in every secretariat and every police station in Kosovo and Metohija. Of course they are now dislocated into Serbia proper, central Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, did you attend to the -- the conclusion of the agreement on the Verification Mission?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I was a member of the delegation of the Republic of Serbia and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia at the negotiations with the representatives of NATO in Belgrade towards the end of summer, the beginning of autumn, 1998. The delegation of NATO was led by Generals Clark and Naumann, and the delegation of the Republic of Yugoslavia and the Republic of Serbia and included several generals of the army, several generals of the police, and some representatives of the state authorities of Serbia and Yugoslavia. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: What were these negotiations about? What was the substance of the negotiations?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The substance of these talks were attempts to agree on a specific reduction of the police force in Kosovo and Metohija and on reducing the activities of the army and the police in time and in territory.
