But we don't know about that now. It is a fact that after brief clashes on the outskirts of the villages --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I asked you specifically about the number. And then could you also tell us about the ethnicity of the civilians. About how many would be with them, they would take?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As a rule, many civilians from the specific settlement. Hardly anybody would stay behind after this kind of a clash with the police once the police would enter the village. Usually when the police would enter the village, there would be no civilians left in the village, and of course no terrorists either. As far as their ethnic background is concerned, they were Albanians for the most part. They would not withdraw into settlements, villages that were not Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: When you say "they" --

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean the terrorists. Of course I mean the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. The civilians that they took with then were for the most part Albanians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. When I said that they attacked from ambushes, I am referring to the well-known principle of hit and run. They were not prepared to remain in combat contact with the units attacked. They would withdraw immediately into villages for the most part. In they would withdraw to areas that were outside settlements, they would remain -- that they would remain in close contact and that -- for a longer period of time and that they could be arrested during the course of that action.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, a very specific question: Did the police open fire at members of the KLA if there was any danger of hurting civilians?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. That was not the policy involved, nor were there such orders involved, nor was that the general thrust.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Is there a single order that you are aware of that gunfire may not be opened if civilians could be hurt?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were several orders that I saw myself, and I think that in these documents there are such orders, but at this moment I cannot find them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. We'll get to that. They were withdrawing, and they were forcing entire villages to withdraw with them. Does that show their awareness that the police would not target civilians or does this show that they think that the police would target civilians?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already explained that, that they were doing that inter alia because they were aware of the fact that the police in such situations did not have the right to fire or did they have any wish to fire or, rather, use firearms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Were you personally ever in a position to see an event of this kind when a number of KLA members were withdrawing with civilians?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say specifically that during 1998, in the summer, after the terrorist incursion in the town of Orahovac and during the police and military operation aimed at the deblockade of the town of Orahovac I was present there and within the operations of the police and the military I was following what was going on in the territory of Orahovac. We saw that a large number of civilians left Orahovac, that they moved towards Malisevo. I myself saw that no one fired at this group of civilians. That was only logical because it was such a big group of civilians. It was quite clear that terrorists were getting out the same way too.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Could you in any way establish whether there were KLA members among the withdrawing civilians?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were at quite a distance, a kilometre away or more, which was too far. But I already explained that terrorists were not wearing uniforms when they were retreating. They would only wear uniforms in Albanian settlements, when they were along roads. When they were clashing with the police they rarely wore uniforms, and if they did, they wore them only briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The example you've given just now relating to Orahovac, did that involve killing of Serb civilians or Serb MUP members; and if so, where is the report into the investigation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The incident involving the capture of Orahovac is a very complex case. From the incursion of terrorists into Orahovac it involved a number of preceding actions in Velika Hoca [phoen], Zociste and a large number of other villages, when just before entering Orahovac the terrrorists kidnapped several dozens of Serb civilians from the said villages, and even the Monks from the monastery in Zociste. Some of those civilians were later found dead, others have not been found to this day and are still missing. In this operation to lift the blockade of Orahovac, the police station was liberated after a blockade and a cut-off of water and other supplies, including food, before the surrounding roads were also deblocked. But I cannot tell you specifically whether a policeman was killed in the operation or not. I believe there were some policemen killed but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, I believe that there are many written records on this incident.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. General, this terrorist organisation called itself an army. Now, in view of your experience, are you in possession of any elements that would support this claim that this was an army?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally am convinced that the so-called KLA never became an army. They indeed had the capacity to mount perfidious hit-and-run attacks, but they were never organised or structured in such a way as to be able to hold a certain territory in a serious military manner and to use that territory as a base from which to mount long-term military operations. I have already said that after short-lived attacks and clashes with the army or the police, they discarded their weapons and uniforms and blended with civilians in order to retreat and avoid arrest.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: From the viewpoint of the attributes that are necessary for a force to be called an army, you've already told us that the KLA could not be an army. Do you know, however, of any case where they honoured and respected international humanitarian law or any other convention that regulated armed conflicts?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was perfectly obvious that the terrorists had no respect for any norms of international law. Earlier today we have analysed many documents that support this conclusion. Most of the victims in terrorist attacks were civilians. Policemen, soldiers and others came second on the list of casualties. But the main casualties were civilians, and that indeed points to the conclusion that they had no respect for international norms of humanitarian law.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: How did you qualify the nature of their attacks on the police?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as attacks on the police are concerned, until the proclamation of the state of war, we categorised them as attacks against civilians although we did not present them as such in statistics, because as long as the police were doing their normal policework without joining any military activities, they can also be considered as civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In your case, is any of these attacks on the police related to an allegation in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, certainly they are, but I haven't come to that yet. I can ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm going to bring the witness to that for that purpose. Or you will ask the witness questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will ask questions of this witness, certainly, among other things about all these allegations concerning alleged crimes listed in various paragraphs of the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, that kind of evidence will be more helpful than the sort of general framework he's outlining as to the pattern of conduct of the KLA. It will be more helpful to your case, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, with regard to what you've just said about the attacks, the terrorist attacks -- let me see. Yes, here it is. What you've just said about civilians being the predominant casualties, does that completely correspond to the charts that we saw in tabs 124 and 126 regarding attacks on civilians versus attacks on policemen, et cetera? Does your testimony completely correspond in this area to the statistics and the charts?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of those pie charts in colour specifically deals with the ratio of civilian victims and the police victims, and it shows clearly that civilians were the predominant casualties of terrorist attacks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And now tell me, were Albanian civilians also the casualties of terrorist attacks in Kosovo and Metohija, the members of their own ethnic community? Let me just draw your attention to this very extensive document under tab 138. But before that, please answer my question: Were Albanians also victims?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to all the operative and other information in the possession of the police, ethnic Albanians were also victims of terrorist activity in Kosovo, members of the Albanian ethnic community. And from the table -- tables we saw, there were many Albanian deaths. And in addition to that, Albanians were, according to police information, recruited by force into the KLA. They were forced to procure and carry weapons, they were forced to do physical labour for the KLA such as building fortifications, engineering work on roads, putting up obstacles, and they were forced to pay money to the KLA to buy weapons, vehicles, and anything else the KLA needed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Under tab 138, it says: "Records of certain items found in KLA headquarters," translated from the original. What does this tab contain?

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This tab contains the documents found during one of the anti-terrorist actions mounted in the village of Leskovac, in the Prizren municipality, and we can see that the date is the 3rd of September, 1998. I have yet to find the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It is somewhere in the middle of this tab, because in the beginning we have facsimiles of these handwritten messages in Albanian.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. And we have translation on pages 1 and 2. This is important in view of the previous answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: There are far more documents than this that are not translated than are translated. It makes it even more difficult to try to compare the originals and the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, tab 138 has been translated. I hope you have the translation. And may I draw your attention to the fact that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Organisation of this is chaotic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we are flooded with the additions throughout the session, and I personally have decided to leave them --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. It's impossible to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- until after to include them in the binders because it's difficult to do that during the case. So we do have a translation. Mr. Milosevic, we have to stop at 1.43 today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The previous page, one page, seems to be page 2 of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, since you have the translation, I will only ask the witness to direct us to some of these documents. They are in the Albanian language, translated into Serbian and translated into English. These documents refer to the pressure exerted on and intimidation of Albanians. They were pressured to do the things that the KLA wanted them to do, as the general just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please explain to us, General, in greater detail.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps the document on page 3 is convenient, if we can all find our way. So the translation is 2/346/98.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Since we have a translation into English, tell us what the Serbian translation says.

utterances.speaker: OBRAD STEVANOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is obviously a threat against the person in the case he does not comply with KLA demands and --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters would appreciate it if the witness would tell us exactly where it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, let us assist the interpreters by telling them exactly where that is. I believe it's the first page, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The third page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The third page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: The third page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the English translation is not sorted in my copy. [In English] "We have concluded that you are ignoring our appeal." [Interpretation] That is the quotation that the witness began to read a moment ago. It is marked in tab 138. It says translation 2/346/98. In the Serbian --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If we are not to trespass on the time of the next case, we will have to adjourn now. We are adjourned until tomorrow, 9.00 a.m.
